subject: Re: Stan code for a complicated model

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Stan code for a complicated model
parts:
On Monday, November 28, 2016 at 11:23:38 AM UTC-5, Tas wrote:
I am fitting a model called ETAS (more in the reference, the kernel is equation 3).  The model has 5 parameters "mu", "k", "p", "c", "alpha". The earthquake magnitudes follow a left-truncated exponential distribution with parameter "beta". I am estimating "beta" together with the 5 parameters of the ETAS model . This "joint estimation" is necessary because to avoid explosive simulation (for later use), the parameters have to satisfy two conditions: 

1) beta> alpha;
2) k*beta/ (beta-alpha) <1.

In the parameters block, do something like

real<lower = 0, upper = 1> k;
real<lower = 0> alpha;
real<lower = alpha, upper = -alpha / (k - 1)> beta;

The restriction that k < 1 may be scientifically wrong. But you need some way of specifying lower and upper bounds on the parameters that can always be satisfied (i.e. lower is always less than upper). And you need a good approximation to that integral in the log-likelihood.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: Stan code for a complicated model
parts:
Dear Ben,

Thanks so much for the help. I removed the "transformed parameters" block and followed your instructions in the "parameters" block. I successfully got the results without any divergent chains (although they did not recover all the parameters). I get this kind of warning message after each chain finishes:


"The following numerical problems occured the indicated number of times after warmup on chain 3
                                                                                                                                                                    count
domain error in lub_constrain;  lower bound = inf must be strictly less than upper bound = inf                     1
When a numerical problem occurs, the Metropolis proposal gets rejected.
However, by design Metropolis proposals sometimes get rejected even when there are no numerical problems.
Thus, if the number in the 'count' column is small, do not ask about this message on stan-users."


I understand that it happens for the change I made in the "parameters" block. So this is not actually an error but it indicates a more accurately specified model. And it occurs for very few number of cases (I got count=1 for most of the chains). But, when the true parameter k is greater than 1, I think, this code will not work. I took an exponential with rate 0.1 for the parameter "alpha". Everything else is same.  Among the 6 parameters, the code recovered:

1) k; beta     in model 1

2) mu; k; p; c in model 2

3)mu, beta     in model 3

.  How can I make a STAN code that will recover parameters for all sets of parameters?

Could you please check?

Tas
